arxiv-2010-09293.title: Privacy-preserving Data Sharing on Vertically Partitioned Data
arxiv-2010-09293.creator: Razane Tajeddine 1 , Joonas Jälkö 2 , Samuel Kaski 2,3 , and Antti Honkela 2 1 Helsinki Institute for Information Technology HIIT, Department of Computer Science, University of Helsinki, Finland 2 Helsinki Institute for Information Technology HIIT, Department of Computer Science, Aalto University, F
arxiv-2010-09293.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce a differentially private method for generating synthetic data from vertically partitioned data, i.e. , where data of the same individuals is distributed across multiple data holders or parties. We present a differentially privacy stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) algorithm to train a mixture model over such partitioned data using variational inference.

arxiv-2103-11932.title: Photoinduced dynamics of organic molecules using nonequilibrium Green’s functions with second-Born, G ​ W GW , T T -matrix and three-particle ladder correlations
arxiv-2103-11932.creator: Y. Pavlyukh, E. Perfetto, G. Stefanucci
arxiv-2103-11932.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Y. Pavlyukh, E. Perfetto, G. Stefanucci. The ultrafast hole dynamics triggered by the photoexcitation of molecular targets is a highly correlated process even for those systems, like organic molecules, having a weakly correlated ground state. We here provide a unifying framework and a numerically efficient matrix formulation of state-of-the-art non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) methods like second-Born as well as G ​ W GW and T T -matrix without and with exchange diagrams.

arxiv-2110-10856.title: The positive Grassmannian, the amplituhedron, and cluster algebras
arxiv-2110-10856.creator: Lauren K. Williams
arxiv-2110-10856.description: Abstract . The positive Grassmannian Gr k , n ≥ 0 \Gr_{k,n}^{\geq 0} is the subset of the real Grassmannian where all Plücker coordinates are nonnegative. It has a beautiful combinatorial structure as well as connections to statistical physics, integrable systems, and scattering amplitudes.

arxiv-2112-12975.title: Identification of misreported beliefs
arxiv-2112-12975.creator: Elias Tsakas
arxiv-2112-12975.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Elias Tsakas. It is well-known that subjective beliefs cannot be identified with traditional choice data unless we impose the strong assumption that preferences are state-independent. This is seen as one of the biggest pitfalls of incentivized belief elicitation. The two common approaches are either to exogenously assume that preferences are state-independent, or to use intractable elicitation mechanisms that require an awful lot of hard-to-get non-traditional choice data.

arxiv-2310-08547.creator: Erik S. Sørensen
arxiv-2310-08547.description: Abstract The screening of an impurity spin in the Kondo model occurs over a characteristic length scale ξ K \xi_{K} , that defines the size of the Kondo screening cloud or “mist”. The presence of such a length scale in experimental and numerical results is rather subtle.

arxiv-2401-17663.description: Abstract The primary aim of this paper is to investigate the integration of emotions into the social navigation framework to analyse its effect on both navigation and human physiological safety and comfort. The proposed framework uses leg detection to find the whereabouts of people and computes adaptive proxemic zones based on their emotional state.

arxiv-2506-10066.title: The LHC as an Axion-Photon Collider
arxiv-2506-10066.creator: Sergio Barbosa, Matheus Coelho, Sylvain Fichet, Gustavo Gil da Silveira, Magno Machado
arxiv-2506-10066.description: Abstract Assuming the existence of an axion-like particle (ALP), beams of relativistic particles emit fluxes of quasi-real ALPs, analogous to the photon fluxes described by Weizsäcker-Williams-type approximations. Consequently, ALP-ALP and ALP-photon collisions can occur at the LHC. We initiate the study of the LHC as an ALP collider, and show that ALP collisions provide competitive probes of certain ALP couplings.

pmc-11356377.description: This study aimed to decipher the influence of red mud on the mechanical properties, pore structure, and microstructure of basic magnesium sulfate cements (BMSCs). The results showed that BMSC prepared with an appropriate addition of red mud exhibited improved mechanical properties and yielded the highest compressive strength of 94.54 MPa after curing for 28 days.

pmc-11535703.title: Microwave imaging for breast cancer screening: protocol for an open, multicentric, interventional, prospective, non-randomised clinical investigation to evaluate cancer detection capabilities of MammoWave system on an asymptomatic population across multiple European countries
pmc-11535703.creator: Daniel Álvarez Sánchez-Bayuela, Juan Fernández Martín, Gianluigi Tiberi, Navid Ghavami, Rubén Giovanetti González, Lina Marcela Cruz Hernánez, Paul Martín Aguilar Angulo, Aarón Darío Martínez Gómez, Ana Rodríguez Sánchez, Alessandra Bigotti, Banafsheh Khalesi, Letizia Pontoriero, Massimo Calabrese,
pmc-11535703.description: IntroductionMicrowave imaging presents several potential advantages including its non-ionising and harmless nature. This open, multicentric, interventional, prospective, non-randomised trial aims to validate MammoWave’s artificial intelligence (AI)-based classification algorithm, leveraging microwave imaging, to achieve a sensitivity exceeding 75% and a specificity exceeding 90% in breast screening.

pmc-11584589.title: Chicken GLUT4 function via enhancing mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and inhibiting ribosome pathway in skeletal muscle satellite cells
pmc-11584589.creator: Lin Zhang, Pengna Luo, Huihong Li, Yuxian Pan, Huaiyong Zhang, Xuemeng Si, Wen Chen, Yanqun Huang
pmc-11584589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Glucose Transporter 4 (GLUT4) is a crucial protein facilitating glucose uptake and metabolism across cell membranes in mammals. However, information on GLUT4 in birds has historically been limited. In this study, we investigated the dynamic expression profile of chicken GLUT4 using real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) and examined its potential effects and mechanisms via GLUT4 overexpression and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) in chicken primary skeletal muscle satellite cells (CP-SMSCs).

pmc-11678662.title: Morphology of the Human Pineal Gland Studied by Freeze-Fracturing in Scanning Electron Microscopy
pmc-11678662.creator: Simona Polakovičová, Ján Líška, Ivan Varga, Paulína Gálfiová, Denis N Silachev
pmc-11678662.description: The human pineal gland is the largest producer of the hormone melatonin. Pineal acervuli (brain sand), calcified concretions in the pineal gland, have long been studied because of their association with ageing, melatonin production, and neurological disorders. The solid inorganic matter of the hydroxyapatite crystals often renders sample sectioning impossible, to the extent that the sections lose value.

pmc-12507943.title: Constant herbivory rates and plant–herbivore interactions along a resource availability gradient in South African fynbos
pmc-12507943.creator: Alexander Neu, Huw Cooksley, Karen J Esler, Anton Pauw, Francois Roets, Frank M Schurr, Matthias Schleuning
pmc-12507943.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Plant–herbivore interactions are important for almost all terrestrial ecosystems, but little is known about how herbivory and the specialization of these interactions change with the resource availability provided by host plant communities and time since disturbance. In fire-prone scrublands of the South African Cape Floristic Region, we studied interaction networks between 20 Protea shrub species and ten herbivorous insect species that consume seeds inside Protea cones during their larval stage.

pmc-12642923.creator: Lucas Sgrott Simão Flausino, Douglas Fernando Kunkel, João Guilherme Cardoso, Lucas Napoli Cordeiro, Kailan Goulart da Silveira, Gabriele Sousa Silval, Maysa Melo Henkes, Fabiana Oenning da Gama, Lucas Sgrott Simão Flausino, Douglas Fernando Kunkel, João Guilherme Cardoso, Lucas Napoli Cordeiro, Kai
pmc-12642923.description: BackgroundChronic Venous Disease (CVD) of the lower extremities (LEs) is a condition with significant prevalence and hospital admission rates.ObjectivesTo analyze temporal trends in hospitalization due to CVD from 2014 to 2023 in Brazil.MethodsAn ecological time series study of CVD-related hospitalization using data from the Brazilian Unified Health System.

pmc-12812726.title: Bariatric surgery as a treatment of polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12812726.creator: Hyder Mirghani, Amani Shaman
pmc-12812726.description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the most common endocrine disorder among females of reproductive age, and the majority are obese/overweight. PCOS management, including lifestyle and drugs, is limited by unsustainability and side effects. Bariatric surgery (BS) is promising in addressing hyperandrogenism and pregnancy outcomes. We aimed to assess the impact of bariatric surgery on PCOS components.

pmc-13144925.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026LB196 INTRA-ARTERIAL ALLOGENIC MESENCHYMAL STEM CELLS (NCS-01) FOLLOWING THROMBECTOMY: PHASE 1 SAFETY, FEASIBILITY, AND EXPLORATORY EFFICACY SIGNALS
pmc-13144925.creator: Dileep Yavagal, Minako Koga, Aaron Rodriguez Calienes, Jason Tarpley, Parita Bhuva, Brian Snelling, Dennis Rivet, Sean Savitz
pmc-13144925.description: Background and aimsDespite treatment advances, a significant proportion of treated patients remain disabled after acute ischaemic stroke (AIS). Endovascularly delivered intra-arterial (IA) mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) may lead to benefit via paracrine-mediated recovery post reperfusion. We aimed to test the safety and exploratory efficacy of dose escalation of NCS-01, an allogeneic bone-marrow-derived MSC sub-population, delivered IA post-thrombectomy.

pmc-13196719.title: Efficacy of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Combined with Exercise in Patients with Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis [Letter]
pmc-13196719.creator: Qunqi Hu, Nisang Chen
pmc-13196719.description: ination of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and exercise for adults with chronic pain, a topic of growing clinical importance. The authors reported small-to-moderate improvements in pain intensity and functional disability, along with benefits in several cognitive-behavioral outcomes, mental health, and quality of life.

pmc-13660328.title: Shikonin-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles mediated magnetothermodynamic therapy with synergistic antibacterial efficacy and immunomodulation for accelerated infected wound healing
pmc-13660328.creator: Jiajun Li, Ning Jiang, Yuqing Miao, Fayi Nie, Jingdu Yang, Xiaohu Mi, Simeng Xue, Yuwei Wu, Tingbin Zhang, Yingxi Duanmiao, Qi Liu, Haiming Fan, Xiaohang Yang, Haifa Qiao
pmc-13660328.description: Infected skin wounds healing remains a great clinical challenge due to the complexity of the wound healing process, involving infection control and subsequent immunomodulation. Magnetothermodynamic (MTD) therapy, combining the magnetothermal effect and thermal-amplified Fenton reactivity, is a promising strategy for combating bacterial infections. However, its therapeutic efficacy in wound healing is compromised due to its insufficient ability to address inflammation.

pmc-13675490.title: Thermal tolerance and acclimation limits in bull trout (Salvelinus confluentus) alevin
pmc-13675490.creator: Brendan Maldonado, Travis Durhack, Andrew Chapelsky, Sarah E Glowa, Analisa Lazaro‐Côté, Raven M Bennett, Timothy Bartley, Neil J Mochnacz
pmc-13675490.description: The critical thermal maximum (CT max) of bull trout (Salvelinus confluentus) alevin was measured after 3 weeks of acclimation to 4–21°C. CT max increased from 24.3 at 4°C to 26.7 at 9°C, plateaued between 9 and 12°C (26.9°C), and declined to 25.9°C at 15°C. Acclimation mortality increased above 12°C, reaching 53.7% at 15°C, and no fish survived at 18–21°C.
